title: Big Brother Season 1: The House That Kept Receipts
subtitle: A season of false counts, broken final twos, public apologies, and one winner who reached the end by surviving the exact weeks that should have exposed him.

winner.name: Wayne
winner.keyStats: Wayne wins Season 1 by a 4–3 jury vote over Priya, with 2 HOH wins, 1 veto win, only 1 nomination, 1 veto save, and zero eviction votes cast against him all season.
winner.strategy: Wayne’s game is built on trust that looks simple until it starts winning votes. He makes people feel protected, lets bigger targets take the heat, and repeatedly positions himself inside overlapping groups without becoming the face of them. When the endgame arrives, he cuts where he has to, owns just enough of it at finale, and benefits from a jury that values the way he handled people on their way out.
winner.legacy: Wayne becomes the season’s first champion by proving that a quiet social game can beat a louder strategic résumé. His win is narrow, emotional, and messy in all the right ways: a 4–3 verdict decided less by one big move than by months of jury management, small kindnesses, and carefully timed survival.

placements.name: Wayne
placements.notes: Wayne wins by making loyalty feel real even when the game forces him to break it.
placements.story: Wayne enters as the sincere one, the player who says he would rather lose as himself than win as somebody else. For weeks, that honesty becomes a shield: Raj trusts him, Priya works with him, and even people who distrust his allies rarely treat Wayne as the immediate problem. His first HOH in Week 5 puts Julia and Bowie on the block and quietly builds the structure that carries him deep. In the endgame, he survives the collapse of old deals, wins the Week 13 HOH, wins the final Part One, and sits beside Priya because she believes his promise is the one worth honoring. At finale, he does not oversell the game; he admits where he followed, where he feared, and where surviving was the move. The jury rewards the person they felt least burned by, and Wayne wins 4–3.
keyMoments: Week 2: Locks in the final two with Raj, giving both players their first real structure.
Week 5: Wins HOH and nominates Julia and Bowie, beginning his visible power game.
Week 10: Votes to evict Caleb’s target Emmah, then watches Priya break the tie.
Week 12: Betrays Raj with his vote, ending the season’s defining loyalty deal.
Week 13: Wins HOH and nominates Hicks and Caleb together to break up a dangerous pair.
Week 15: Wins the veto and casts the sole vote to evict Caleb, the season’s comp giant.
Finale: Wins Part One, loses Part Three, then beats Priya 4–3 with jury respect and social capital.

placements.name: Priya
placements.notes: Priya plays the cleanest strategic game on paper, but the jury makes her pay for the relationships she turned into moves.
placements.story: Priya spends the early game counting messes, votes, and relationships with the same terrifying precision. She survives two nominations, wins two HOHs and two vetoes, and repeatedly uses power to pull the season toward the endgame she wants. Her Week 10 HOH removes Emmah on a tie-breaker, and her veto saves Zee in Week 9, proving she will spend capital when the relationship matters. But the same controlled game that gets her to the final chair also leaves jurors questioning whether her loyalty was ever more than positioning. At Final Three, she wins the last HOH and cuts Zee, the decision that proves she is playing to win rather than to be loved. She loses 4–3 to Wayne, close enough to haunt the season, but strong enough that even Caleb votes for the game she played.
keyMoments: Week 4: Publicly names the wrong saboteur and spends her one official accusation on Hicks.
Week 8: Wins veto and uses it on Damien, forcing Bowie into the replacement chair.
Week 9: Wins veto again and saves Zee, sending MK to the block instead.
Week 10: Wins HOH, nominates Bowie and Emmah, then breaks the tie to evict Emmah.
Week 13: Survives the block against Hicks after the house chooses to keep her threat level in play.
Week 15: Wins HOH at Final Four and nominates Zee and Caleb together.
Finale: Wins the final HOH, cuts Zee, and loses the jury vote 4–3.

placements.name: Zee
placements.notes: Zee survives four nominations, two veto saves around him, and a collapsing web of deals before one final decision leaves him third.
placements.story: Zee starts as the friendly connective tissue of the house, then gradually becomes someone everyone realizes is connected to everyone else. He touches the block four times and keeps finding a way back into the room, often by letting others become the emergency. His relationships with Emmah, Priya, Caleb, Brightly, and later Wayne give him options, but those same overlapping promises become impossible to manage. In Week 14, he wins HOH and takes the shot that sends Damien to jury, but the decision exposes just how many final twos he has promised. At Final Three, he pitches Priya on loyalty and jury respect, but admits he would have taken Wayne himself. Priya cuts him, and he becomes the final juror with no votes at the end but a massive footprint on the season.
keyMoments: Week 2: Survives the block against Millie after a messy 9–5 vote.
Week 9: Priya uses the veto on him, proving their bond has real game value.
Week 12: Survives against Raj after Wayne and Priya help flip the vote.
Week 13: His relationship with Priya becomes public and increasingly dangerous.
Week 14: Wins HOH and nominates Wayne and Priya, then breaks the tie to evict Damien.
Week 15: Survives the sole vote when Wayne evicts Caleb instead.
Finale: Loses Part Two to Priya and is cut at Final Three.

placements.name: Caleb
placements.notes: Caleb dominates veto competitions and becomes America’s Favourite, but his jury threat finally becomes too large to hide.
placements.story: Caleb is the season’s engine: visible, emotional, competitive, and constantly in motion. He wins five vetoes and one HOH, saving himself from the block three times and turning danger into spectacle. His Week 8 HOH targets Brightly and Damien, but his bigger story is the repeated scramble after being nominated five times. By the endgame, everyone knows the same truth: if Caleb reaches the final chairs, the jury may reward the fight. Wayne gets the only vote at Final Four and takes the shot, evicting Caleb 1–0 after Caleb pleads with the weight of six competition wins behind him. He leaves hurt, wrong about who made it happen, and then wins America’s Favourite Houseguest by a wide margin.
keyMoments: Week 3: Wins his first veto in Cold Comfort and chooses not to use it.
Week 8: Wins HOH in Rollin' in the Dough and nominates Brightly and Damien.
Week 10: Survives the block when Priya breaks a tie against Emmah.
Week 11: Wins veto with his own game at risk and keeps nominations the same.
Week 12: Wins veto in The Black Box and saves himself, forcing Raj up.
Week 13: Wins the Final Six veto and saves himself again.
Week 15: Is evicted 1–0 by Wayne despite being the season’s biggest comp résumé.

placements.name: Damien
placements.notes: Damien plays a perceptive, relationship-heavy game that reaches Final Five before one tie-breaker ends it.
placements.story: Damien spends much of the season as the person people trust in quiet rooms. He rarely needs power early, because his influence lives in late-night talks, calm reads, and the ability to make people feel heard. His Week 12 HOH is his one direct reign, and he uses it to nominate Caleb and Zee with Raj waiting as the replacement target. But his position depends on relationships that are also working against each other, especially with Priya, Zee, and Wayne. At Final Five, he lands on the block beside Priya after Caleb saves Wayne, and the vote splits 1–1. Zee breaks the tie against him, ending the run of a player who often knew the room was changing but waited one conversation too long.
keyMoments: Week 4: Builds trust with Priya after a private emotional moment.
Week 8: Is nominated by Caleb, then saved by Priya’s veto.
Week 10: Votes to keep Emmah in the 3–3 tie that Priya breaks.
Week 12: Wins HOH and nominates Caleb and Zee.
Week 12: Renominates Raj after Caleb uses the veto, setting up Raj’s eviction.
Week 14: Is forced onto the block as the only replacement after Caleb uses the veto on Wayne.
Week 14: Is evicted on Zee’s tie-breaking vote against Priya.

placements.name: Hicks
placements.notes: Hicks builds strong rooms and sharp reads, but his late-game safety disappears the moment Wayne turns power on him.
placements.story: Hicks is one of the house’s earliest information brokers, the player who watches more than he talks and usually knows which conversation mattered. He wins HOH in Week 3 and Week 11, both times using power to shape the board while keeping multiple alliances alive. His relationships with Brightly, Raj, Caleb, and Priya give him reach, but also make him a common suspect whenever numbers fail to add up. In Week 13, Wayne nominates Hicks beside Caleb to expose the Caleb-Hicks connection, and Caleb’s veto win leaves Hicks sitting next to Priya. Hicks campaigns with logic, but the house chooses to keep Priya’s endgame value over his network. He leaves in sixth, angry but respected, believing Wayne masterminded the week even as the vote came from elsewhere.
keyMoments: Week 3: Wins HOH and nominates Nichelle and MK.
Week 3: Keeps nominations intact after Caleb wins veto, leading to Nichelle’s eviction.
Week 7: Survives the block against Chase by a single vote.
Week 11: Wins HOH and nominates Bowie and Raj.
Week 11: Watches Bowie leave unanimously while Raj survives as the pawn.
Week 13: Is nominated by Wayne beside Caleb.
Week 13: Is evicted 2–1 against Priya after Caleb saves himself.

placements.name: Raj
placements.notes: Raj’s loyalty makes him powerful, then predictable, and finally expendable.
placements.story: Raj begins with a simple promise: whoever he rides with, he rides the whole way. That promise becomes his season with Wayne, and for a long stretch it gives both players cover, certainty, and a clear endgame shape. He wins HOH in Week 2, wins veto in Week 6, and survives four nominations by leaning on trust more than campaigning. But as the house shrinks, everyone can see where Raj’s vote lives before he casts it. In Week 12, Damien uses Caleb and Zee as the opening nominees and Raj as the replacement, putting loyalty itself on trial. Wayne, Priya, and Caleb all break promises to vote him out, and Raj becomes the third juror with one of the season’s most painful exits.
keyMoments: Week 2: Wins HOH and nominates Brightly and Zee.
Week 2: Names Millie as replacement after Brightly uses the veto.
Week 5: Formalizes a final three with Wayne and Priya.
Week 6: Wins veto and saves himself from Bowie’s nominations.
Week 9: Survives against MK after Priya’s veto creates the replacement nomination.
Week 11: Survives unanimously against Bowie as Hicks’s pawn.
Week 12: Is renominated after Caleb wins veto and is evicted 3–1.

placements.name: Bowie
placements.notes: Bowie is the season’s great tactician until his threat level finally becomes too obvious to protect.
placements.story: Bowie walks in pretending to want jury and a hot tub, then immediately starts counting the house better than most people count votes. He wins three HOHs and two vetoes, repeatedly making the week about other people’s mistakes while pushing his own targets forward. His Week 4 HOH backdoors Ripper, and his Week 6 HOH removes Scary Girl, but every win adds another layer to the target. Bowie survives five nominations, saves himself twice with veto power, and keeps inventing stories long enough for some of them to become useful. By Week 11, Hicks puts him up next to Raj, and the remaining players agree that Bowie has too many paths to the end. He leaves 5–0, becomes a sharp jury voice, and later helps shape Wayne’s winning coalition.
keyMoments: Week 4: Wins HOH and nominates Caleb and Chase.
Week 4: Uses Julia’s veto outcome to renom Ripper and send him out 10–2.
Week 6: Wins HOH and nominates Scary Girl and Raj.
Week 7: Wins veto while nominated and forces Chase into the replacement chair.
Week 9: Wins HOH and nominates Zee and Raj, with MK as the real backdoor target.
Week 10: Wins veto while on the block and forces Caleb into danger.
Week 11: Is evicted 5–0 against Raj after Hicks’s HOH.

placements.name: Emmah
placements.notes: Emmah plays loud, precise, and personal, becoming the first juror after Priya breaks a tie against her.
placements.story: Emmah begins the season on the Week 1 block and survives because the house decides Axel is the bigger problem. From there, she becomes one of the season’s emotional pressure points: direct, confrontational, and impossible to ignore. Her Week 7 HOH is the peak of her power and the start of her downfall, as she nominates Hicks and Bowie and makes the Hicks feud unmistakably personal. She stays protected through deals with Zee, Damien, and Wayne, but the web stops holding when Priya wins Week 10 HOH. After Bowie saves himself with the veto, Emmah sits beside Caleb and the house splits 3–3. Priya breaks the tie against her, making Emmah the first juror and the first major warning that endgame relationships will not save everyone.
keyMoments: Week 1: Survives the instant eviction against Axel by a 13–2 vote.
Week 2: Forms a final three with Damien and Zee.
Week 7: Wins the endurance HOH on The Wall.
Week 7: Nominates Hicks and Bowie and makes the week openly personal.
Week 10: Is nominated by Priya beside Bowie.
Week 10: Faces Caleb after Bowie’s veto and loses on Priya’s tie-breaker.
Week 10: Enters jury as its first member.

placements.name: MK
placements.notes: MK gathers information everywhere, but her social web snaps after Chase leaves and Priya makes her the replacement target.
placements.story: MK spends the early weeks as a subtle collector of promises, rumors, and small obligations. She survives the block in Week 3, wins the Week 5 veto, and becomes central to several overlapping structures, including the Chase relationship that the house never stops watching. Her biggest strength is also her liability: people know she knows too much. After Chase is evicted, MK’s position becomes harder to defend, and her attempts to redirect the house start looking like damage control. In Week 9, Priya saves Zee with the veto and Bowie names MK as the replacement nominee. Against Raj, the house decides MK has more ways to damage them than protect them, and she leaves 6–1.
keyMoments: Week 3: Survives the block against Nichelle after a 10–3 vote.
Week 4: Helps the Ripper vote come together and owns it in goodbye messages.
Week 5: Wins the Tower of Hanoi veto and chooses not to use it.
Week 6: Survives as Bowie’s replacement nominee against Scary Girl.
Week 7: Votes out Chase despite their showmance, creating one of the season’s messiest emotional breaks.
Week 9: Is renominated after Priya saves Zee with the veto.
Week 9: Is evicted 6–1 against Raj.

placements.name: Brightly
placements.notes: Brightly sees the shape of the house early, but too many side deals make them impossible to keep.
placements.story: Brightly plays the first half like someone solving the season from inside the walls. They win the Week 2 veto when they need it, come off the block, and immediately become a player people both need and distrust. Their ties to Hicks, Caleb, Zee, Chase, and later Raj give them options, but the options begin contradicting one another in public. By Week 8, Caleb nominates Brightly beside Damien, and Priya’s veto saves Damien, leaving Bowie as the replacement. Brightly argues that Bowie is the bigger competition threat, but the house has grown tired of wondering which version of Brightly is true. They leave 5–3, one week before jury, with more correct reads than usable votes.
keyMoments: Week 2: Wins the Power of Veto and saves themselves from Raj’s nominations.
Week 2: Watches Millie become the replacement and leave 9–5.
Week 3: Becomes central to the Wildcard Pact and Undertow overlap.
Week 5: Survives Wayne’s HOH from off the block while Julia leaves.
Week 7: Votes out Chase despite their final three, breaking a major promise.
Week 8: Is nominated by Caleb beside Damien.
Week 8: Is evicted 5–3 against Bowie.

placements.name: Chase
placements.notes: Chase is the saboteur, the early social connector, and the pre-jury player whose secret war bends the season without saving him.
placements.story: Chase enters as a friendly improviser and secretly becomes the saboteur, taking missions that make the house distrust itself before it ever fully understands him. He helps build the Dock Pact, drifts into the Merge Mob, and develops a public relationship with MK that makes both of them easier to target. His sabotage succeeds twice, including the memory wall stunt and the campaign disruption that helps doom Ripper. But once the twist pays out in Week 5, his mystery value disappears and his social debts remain. In Week 7, Emmah’s HOH puts Hicks and Bowie up, Bowie saves himself, and Chase becomes the replacement nominee. He loses 5–4 to Hicks, one vote short of jury, leaving several houseguests to realize too late how much he shaped.
keyMoments: Week 1: Accepts the first saboteur mission and is spotted by Zee.
Week 3: Successfully wrecks the week by flipping the memory wall photos.
Week 4: Breaks Ripper’s campaign by arriving in rooms before him.
Week 5: Is publicly revealed as the saboteur and banks $10,000.
Week 6: Survives as the social center of the MK showmance.
Week 7: Is renominated after Bowie uses veto on himself.
Week 7: Is evicted 5–4 against Hicks.

placements.name: Scary Girl
placements.notes: Scary Girl is underestimated as chaos until the house realizes chaos still counts as a vote.
placements.story: Scary Girl begins as an unpredictable presence, recruited into early groups but rarely made central to the plan. She survives the first waves by being useful enough, strange enough, and not quite dangerous enough to unite the house. Her Week 6 nomination beside Raj becomes the first time the room openly treats her as the problem rather than the accessory. Raj wins veto, MK goes up, and Scary Girl’s campaign cannot overcome the house’s desire for stability. She leaves 8–2, angry and convinced Bowie was the architect, when the deeper machinery was spread across several rooms.
keyMoments: Week 1: Joins The Dock Pact after being brought into the bedroom.
Week 4: Votes out Ripper after promising the move, helping end The Dock Pact era.
Week 5: Is moved by Julia’s final plea but still lands on the wrong side of the read.
Week 6: Is nominated by Bowie beside Raj.
Week 6: Watches Raj win veto and MK take the replacement chair.
Week 6: Is evicted 8–2 against MK.

placements.name: Julia
placements.notes: Julia plays openly, sharply, and too visibly, leaving after Wayne’s HOH turns her own momentum against her.
placements.story: Julia is one of the first people to speak after the twist and one of the first people to make the house nervous. She wins the Week 4 veto, saves Caleb, and accidentally helps create the opening that sends Ripper out instead. Her problem is never a lack of plan; it is that the Diary Room hears the plan before the house does. In Week 5, Wayne nominates Julia beside Bowie, and Julia spends the week trying to turn the vote into a referendum on bigger threats. Her final plea moves Scary Girl live, but it is not enough. She leaves 7–4, dropping true information about Priya and Wayne on the way out and changing how the house watches them afterward.
keyMoments: Week 1: Breaks the twist silence and immediately marks herself as fearless.
Week 4: Wins the Pure Chance veto.
Week 4: Uses the veto on Caleb, allowing Ripper to be renominated.
Week 5: Is nominated by Wayne beside Bowie.
Week 5: Moves Scary Girl with her final plea, but cannot flip the vote.
Week 5: Is evicted 7–4 and exposes the Priya-Wayne connection at the door.

placements.name: Ripper
placements.notes: Ripper thinks silence means safety until the entire house votes like the conversation already happened without him.
placements.story: Ripper starts loud, physical, and convinced that not having a strategy might somehow become one. He helps form The Dock Pact, then The Undertow, but quickly becomes the member people talk around instead of with. In Week 4, Bowie’s HOH sets up Caleb and Chase, Julia’s veto saves Caleb, and Ripper is the replacement target waiting in the plan. The saboteur quietly wrecks his campaign, arriving before him in rooms and leaving him wondering why every answer feels pre-decided. Ripper barely campaigns because he miscounts the danger, and the house evicts him 10–2. He leaves believing Bowie made it happen, which is only partly the story and not the secret that mattered.
keyMoments: Week 1: Forms The Dock Pact with Chase.
Week 2: Forms The Undertow with Hicks.
Week 3: Is pulled deeper into overlapping alliances that never fully protect him.
Week 4: Is renominated after Julia saves Caleb with the veto.
Week 4: Has his campaign quietly disrupted by Chase’s saboteur mission.
Week 4: Is evicted 10–2 against Chase.

placements.name: Nichelle
placements.notes: Nichelle’s social subtlety keeps her alive early, but once she hits the block she cannot rebuild the vote fast enough.
placements.story: Nichelle enters trying not to be noticed, but her real game is in the personal conversations people mistake for downtime. She builds trust with Zee and finds herself close enough to the action to see patterns before others do. Hicks nominates her beside MK in Week 3, and Nichelle correctly argues that the vote says more about alliances than about nominees. Her final plea moves Chase live, proving she can still change minds under pressure. But the larger rooms have already decided, and the vote lands 10–3 against her. She leaves pre-jury convinced Brightly’s comfort gave the game away, and in many ways her read is better than her position.
keyMoments: Week 1: Builds an early connection with Damien and later Zee.
Week 2: Performs strongly in Caged Eggs but remains socially adrift.
Week 3: Is nominated by Hicks beside MK.
Week 3: Exposes how much of the house is moving without her.
Week 3: Moves Chase with her final plea in the living room.
Week 3: Is evicted 10–3 against MK.

placements.name: Millie
placements.notes: Millie wins the first HOH, makes the first irreversible move, and pays for it one week later.
placements.story: Millie’s season burns bright and short. She wins the instant Week 1 HOH, is locked away from the house, and nominates Axel and Emmah with no veto available and no time to soften the blow. Axel leaves, but everyone remembers that Millie’s power had no conversation attached to it. In Week 2, Raj nominates Brightly and Zee, Brightly wins veto, and Millie becomes the replacement nominee. Caleb tries to save her through the Wildcard Pact, but the vote fractures and comes back 9–5 against her. She exits warning people to compare notes, which becomes the season’s most useful advice far too late.
keyMoments: Week 1: Wins the first HOH in the instant eviction format.
Week 1: Nominates Axel and Emmah without any veto in play.
Week 1: Watches Axel leave 13–2 and inherits the consequences.
Week 2: Is renominated after Brightly saves themselves with veto.
Week 2: Loses the Wildcard Pact numbers she thought she had.
Week 2: Is evicted 9–5 against Zee.

placements.name: Axel
placements.notes: Axel’s bluntness makes her the first easy consensus target in a house desperate for one.
placements.story: Axel enters with force, honesty, and a short fuse that the house immediately understands how to use. The instant eviction twist gives her no veto and almost no time to reframe the story after early conflict with Emmah. Millie names Axel and Emmah from a locked HOH room, and the house hears the reasoning before Millie even returns downstairs. Axel campaigns with the argument that she is direct and useful, but the house decides direct danger is still danger. She is evicted 13–2, leaving angry and convinced Emmah did it to her. The season’s first exit becomes the template for weeks of people voting based on comfort as much as strategy.
keyMoments: Week 1: Clashes with Emmah over food and becomes the house’s first loud story.
Week 1: Is nominated by Millie during the instant eviction.
Week 1: Has no veto available and no full week to campaign.
Week 1: Pitches herself as direct danger the house can use.
Week 1: Is evicted 13–2 against Emmah.

seasonNarrative: Season 1 is a house built on bad information. The saboteur twist poisons the early weeks, not because Chase earns the most money, but because everyone starts believing the wrong person at the wrong time. Early power swings are brutal: Millie wins an instant HOH and leaves the next week, Raj exposes his Wayne bond too soon, and Bowie becomes the season’s first true tactician by weaponizing rooms, rumors, and replacement nominations. The middle game is a maze of alliances with names that stop meaning what they used to mean: The Undertow, The Wildcard Pact, The Signal, The Guard, and The Outwit Club all protect people until the vote count says they do not. Caleb becomes the comp monster, Priya becomes the strategist, Zee becomes the social survivor, and Wayne becomes the player jurors keep forgiving. By the end, nearly every finalist has betrayed somebody on the jury, but Wayne’s betrayals feel less like contempt and more like survival. Priya wins the final HOH and cuts Zee, the most personal move of the season, only to lose 4–3 to Wayne. It is a season decided by one vote, but built by a hundred small conversations nobody thought mattered at the time.

bestStrategic.name: Priya
bestStrategic.description: Priya repeatedly turned danger into position: saving Zee with veto, removing Emmah on a tie, cutting Zee at Final Three, and reaching the final two with one of the strongest strategic résumés in the house.

bestSocial.name: Wayne
bestSocial.description: Wayne’s social game survived broken promises that should have ended him. Jurors kept finding reasons to respect him, forgive him, or at least believe he saw them as people before he saw them as votes.

bestPhysical.name: Caleb
bestPhysical.description: Caleb was the season’s defining competition force, especially in veto rounds where danger followed him and he kept winning anyway.

mostClutch.name: Caleb
mostClutch.description: When Caleb’s name hit the block, he repeatedly answered with veto wins, including the late-game saves in Weeks 12 and 13 that forced the house to find someone else.

mostLoyal.name: Wayne
mostLoyal.description: Wayne did break promises, but the reason his game worked is that people experienced him as loyal long before they experienced him as dangerous. That perception won him Zee, Damien, Emmah, and Raj’s respect when it mattered.

bestUnderdog.name: Zee
bestUnderdog.description: Zee was nominated four times, misread by allies, exposed in multiple deals, and still reached Final Three by keeping himself socially useful after every collapse.

biggestVillain.name: Bowie
biggestVillain.description: Bowie lied cleanly, counted coldly, and turned rumors into weapons. Even when he apologized, the house could feel him measuring the next vote.

mostChaotic.name: Chase
mostChaotic.description: Chase’s saboteur run made the whole house worse at trusting its own eyes, and his personal game added a showmance, broken alliances, and one of the season’s closest pre-jury votes.

quietestThreat.name: Damien
quietestThreat.description: Damien rarely needed to be the loudest person in the room. His influence lived in private trust, careful timing, and the way people kept realizing too late that he had been in the room for everything.

seasonMVP.name: Wayne
seasonMVP.description: Wayne won the season by combining enough power, enough honesty, and enough jury goodwill to beat a sharper strategist in a one-vote finish.

mostTragic.name: Raj
mostTragic.description: Raj’s whole identity was loyalty, and his eviction was caused by the exact people whose loyalty he trusted most: Wayne, Priya, and Caleb.

mostUnlucky.name: Bowie
mostUnlucky.description: Bowie won plenty, but his timing was brutal: every successful move made him more obvious, and by Week 11 the whole house agreed his résumé could not be allowed to continue.

ironPerson.name: Caleb
ironPerson.description: Five nominations, five veto wins, three times saved off the block, and constant pressure made Caleb the season’s endurance story even outside the endurance comps.

biggestMeltdown.name: Emmah
biggestMeltdown.description: Emmah’s Week 7 HOH speech made the Hicks nomination openly personal, and the room immediately recalculated her threat level.

gold.name: Wayne
gold.description: The winner, the jury manager, and the player whose endgame answers matched the season the jury lived through.

silver.name: Priya
silver.description: The strategic runner-up whose decisions shaped the boot order, even if the final jury preferred Wayne’s relationships.

gold.name: Wayne
gold.description: Wayne was the emotional center of the winning story: flawed, sincere, and still willing to admit the parts of his game that were not heroic.

silver.name: Caleb
silver.description: Caleb’s fight from the block and his America’s Favourite win made him the audience’s most watchable hero, even when the house feared him.

gold.name: Bowie
gold.description: Bowie made the most visible strategic messes: planted stories, public exposures, and HOH weeks designed to make other people own his moves.

silver.name: MK
silver.description: MK’s information game and willingness to let others take the blame made her one of the season’s most dangerous social operators.

gold.name: Caleb
gold.description: Six total competition wins, including five vetoes, made Caleb the standard every late-game player measured their threat level against.

silver.name: Bowie
silver.description: Three HOHs and two vetoes gave Bowie the second-most intimidating competition résumé and made his eviction feel inevitable.

gold.name: Wayne
gold.description: Wayne won because jurors felt the relationship even after the betrayal. That is the social game in its hardest form.

silver.name: Zee
silver.description: Zee kept doors open with warmth, humor, and personal bonds long after his strategic position should have collapsed.

gold.name: Priya
gold.description: Priya’s path to the end was built through veto timing, tie-breaking, threat management, and a final cut that proved she understood win equity.

silver.name: Bowie
silver.description: Bowie’s best weeks were chessboards: nominees as decoys, replacements as targets, and rumors as leverage.

gold.name: Caleb
gold.description: Caleb survived the block all season with vetoes and charm, then left at Final Four on Wayne’s lone vote after believing that relationship was real.

silver.name: Raj
silver.description: Raj was evicted by Wayne, Priya, and Caleb after trusting all three, turning loyalty into the season’s most painful liability.

gold.name: Chase
gold.description: Chase’s saboteur role warped the first month, earned money, and sent the house into false accusations that outlived the twist itself.

silver.name: Priya
silver.description: Priya’s best advantage was veto control: she used power at exactly the moments that protected her preferred endgame.

gold.name: Caleb
gold.description: Caleb had the competition résumé, the audience support, and multiple jurors arguing his case, but one Final Four vote kept him out of the chairs.

gold.name: Wayne
gold.description: Wayne’s finale performance worked because he did not overclaim. He admitted fear, survival, and following when necessary, which made the jury believe the rest of his case.

gold.name: Priya
gold.description: Priya lost by one vote after controlling several of the season’s most important turns, including Emmah’s eviction, Zee’s save, and the final cut.

messiestFeud.description: What began as irritation over space, pans, and respect became one of the season’s longest strategic fault lines, with both players using the feud as proof the other had to go.

biggestBetrayal.description: Wayne had a late final two with Caleb, won the only veto vote at Final Four, and evicted him anyway, cutting the season’s biggest comp threat one step from finale night.

secondBiggestBetrayal.description: Priya had a final three with Raj, then voted him out when the numbers demanded it, helping destroy one of the season’s oldest loyalty structures.

legacyMoment.name: Priya cuts Zee at Final Three
legacyMoment.description: Priya wins the final HOH and chooses Wayne over Zee, ending her most personal relationship in the game and setting up the 4–3 jury verdict that defines the season.

fanFavorite.name: Caleb
fanFavorite.description: Caleb was voted the house's favourite by the audience.
